主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has adopted rules to modernize and simplify disclosure requirements for public companies, investment advisers, and investment companies, as mandated by the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation (FAST) Act. These amendments aim to eliminate outdated and unnecessary disclosures, improve readability and navigability of company disclosures, and reduce the burden on registrants. Key changes include increased flexibility in discussing historical periods in Management’s Discussion and Analysis, the ability to redact confidential information from most exhibits without a confidential treatment request, and the incorporation of technology to enhance access to information on the cover page of filings. The amendments will take effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, with some provisions, such as data tagging and HTML formatting, having specific effective dates. The SEC emphasized that these changes will benefit investors by improving transparency and reducing costs. The SEC has adopted rules to implement the FAST Act mandate, aiming to modernize and simplify disclosure processes. The requirements for tagging data on the cover pages of certain filings are subject to a three-year phase-in period, depending on the nature of the filer. All investment company registration statements and Form N-CSR filings made on or after April 1, 2020, must be submitted in HTML format and comply with the rule and form amendments related to the use of hyperlinks. This update is part of the SEC's ongoing efforts to enhance transparency and efficiency in financial disclosures. The final rule was published in the Federal Register on March 20, 2019.
